questions.q: What does hierarchical namespace actually maintain internally?
options: A real directory index, separate from the blobs themselves, tracking which directories exist and how they nest
A second copy of every blob for backup purposes
A list of every user who has ever accessed the account
Nothing — it's a purely cosmetic labeling feature
questions.explain: This index is what makes directory-level operations atomic instead of requiring a scan across matching blobs.

questions.q: What are the three steps of the official Data Lake Gen2 migration?
options: Review account changes, Validate account, then Upgrade account
Backup, Delete, Recreate
Create a new account, copy data, delete the old account
There is only one step: click Upgrade
questions.explain: Each step must pass before the next runs — it's a real, gated process, not a single click.

questions.q: Is the Data Lake Gen2 upgrade reversible?
options: No — it's one-way, and Microsoft recommends validating it in a non-production environment first
Yes, it can be undone at any time from the same blade
Yes, but only within 24 hours
Reversibility depends on the Azure region
questions.explain: Once upgraded, there's no supported path back to a Blob-only account.

questions.q: Name two features that must be disabled before the upgrade will pass validation.
options: Blob snapshots and soft delete (for blobs or containers) — along with encryption scopes and immutable storage
Storage account name and region
Performance tier and redundancy level
Container names and directory paths
questions.explain: These specific features block the validation step if left enabled, and must be turned off first.

questions.q: Why is deciding hierarchical namespace at creation time (Lesson 2's checkbox) usually the better choice?
options: It avoids every constraint of the official upgrade path entirely — no one-way migration, no features to disable, no validation risk
It's the only way hierarchical namespace can ever be enabled
Creating at creation time is actually more restrictive than upgrading later
There is no difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: The upgrade path is a safety net for data already in a Blob-only account, not a reason to defer the decision.
